situation: Junior on my team, Nadia, handled a tense call with our client Brightwell today. They pushed hard on the delay and she gave them the new date and the reason in two sentences, and they settled right down. Want to tell her on Slack.
reply: Nadia, the way you handled the Brightwell call today was great. When they pushed on the delay, you gave them the new date and the reason in two sentences and they settled right down. I'm borrowing that.

situation: 领导王总在部门群里夸我这次展会方案做得好，其实是我和小周一起做的，物料和现场流程主要是她负责。怎么回比较得体？
reply: 谢谢王总！这次确实花了不少心思，看到效果挺开心的。物料和现场流程小周出了很多力，这份功劳有她一半。
note: 先大方接住，再提同事，不要一上来就说"没有没有，都是大家的功劳"。

situation: I'm a contractor redoing a client's kitchen. This morning he texted 'you look great in those overalls ha', the first comment like that. I want to keep it from becoming a thing without losing the job; countertop templating is booked for Thursday at 9.
reply: Ha, thanks. Back to the job: countertop templating is booked for Thursday at 9.
note: First time: light, short and closed, with nothing to build on. If it repeats, say plainly you'd rather keep things to the project and keep the messages; if you ever feel unsafe on site, leave and call emergency services.

situation: When I was in hospital for 5 days in August, my neighbour Glen walked and fed my dog Biscuit twice a day without me having to ask twice. Now I'm back on my feet I want to send him a proper thank-you text.
reply: Glen, I've been meaning to say this properly. When I was in hospital in August, knowing you were walking and feeding Biscuit twice a day meant I could actually rest instead of lying there worrying. You're a brilliant neighbour. Thank you, truly.
note: What he did, what it made possible, one line about him, and no favour or gift attached, so it stays a thank-you.

situation: Our VP, Carla, ran the all-hands today about the reorg and answered every hard question straight, including admitting she got the timing of the announcement wrong. I'm two levels below her. I want to send a short message without sounding like I'm sucking up.
reply: Carla, thank you for today's all-hands. When you said you got the timing of the announcement wrong, it made everything else you said much easier to trust.
note: To someone senior: short, one specific moment and its effect, and nothing asked in return.

situation: 儿子乐乐上二年级，开学时每天早上哭着不肯去。班主任刘老师这一个月每天在校门口接他，还让他当了图书角管理员，现在他天天催着出门。想在微信上好好谢谢刘老师。
reply: 刘老师，想正式跟您说声谢谢。开学那几周乐乐每天早上都哭，您每天在门口接他，还让他管图书角，现在他每天早上催着我出门。这一个月的变化我们在家看得特别清楚，您真的很用心。
note: 感谢要具体：她做了什么、带来了什么变化、一句关于她本人；不附带任何请求。

situation: I told Ben, a colleague on another team, that his talk at the product offsite was the clearest explanation of our pricing I'd ever heard. He DM'd back 'haha careful, people will think you're flirting'. I'm married and it really wasn't that. We work together on a project next month.
reply: Ha, no angle here, I just thought your talk was the clearest explanation of our pricing I've heard and wanted to say so.
note: Clarify in one plain line without apologising for the compliment, then restate the specific thing so it stays about the work.

situation: My friend Hana played her first open mic on Saturday and was genuinely great, especially her own song about her grandmother. I texted her that and she replied 'omg no, I was so off-key in the second verse, it was a mess'.
reply: I mean it, that song about your grandmother was genuinely great, second verse and all. Nice work.
note: When they deflect, don't argue them into accepting it. Repeat it once, shorter, and leave it.

situation: My mom, Linda Price, was on the cardiac ward at St. Luke's for 9 days in September. One nurse, Joanne, explained every medication to her in plain words and came back after her shift ended to check on her the night before surgery. I'm Emma, and I want to email Joanne and copy her ward manager.
reply: Dear Joanne, I wanted to thank you for how you cared for my mother, Linda Price, on the cardiac ward in September. You explained every new medication to her in plain words, and the night before her surgery you came back after your shift had ended just to check on her. That kind of care is something our family won't forget. Thank you. With gratitude, Emma Price
note: Copying the manager makes the thanks count where it matters to her; keep it to what she did and what it changed, with nothing asked.

situation: 姑姑在家族群里发了我们国庆前聚会的照片，还@我说'瘦了好多，比以前好看多了！'。其实我是前段时间生病才瘦的，不想在群里解释，也不想冷场。
reply: 谢谢姑姑！我现在挺好的。这张照片大家都笑得很开心，我也存下来了。
note: 收下好意，不解释原因，也不纠正她；一句感谢加一句关于照片的话就够了，病情可以只和想说的人私下讲。

situation: My wife Maya hosted her first Diwali dinner last night, 14 people including my parents. She made my dad his own mild dal because he can't do spice, and my mum said in the car it was the best Diwali she's had in years. I want to text Maya today.
reply: Maya, I keep thinking about last night. You cooked for fourteen, and you remembered Dad can't do spice and made him his own dal. Mum told me in the car it was the best Diwali she's had in years. I'm so proud of you.
note: Partners get generic praise most of all; name the choices she made and pass on the effect, with nothing attached.

situation: My 15-year-old son Eli's team lost the county basketball semi-final on Saturday by four points. He barely scored, but every time one of the younger players missed, he was the first to pick them up and talk them back into it. He's been gloomy since and I want to text him.
reply: Eli, I keep thinking about Saturday. Every time one of the younger guys missed, you were the first one there, pulling him up and talking him back into the game. That's the kind of teammate people remember, and I was really proud watching it.
note: Praise the choice he made, not the score, and keep any 'next time' advice out of the same message.

situation: Aisha, who has reported to me for three years, is leaving for a job in Lisbon. On Slack today she wrote 'you're honestly the best manager I've ever had, I learned so much from you'. I tend to brush this stuff off and I don't want to this time.
reply: Thank you, Aisha, that really means a lot, and this time I'm going to take it rather than brush it off. Keep in touch, I want to hear how Lisbon goes.
note: Receiving praise from someone junior: accept it plainly and don't bounce it straight back; save your praise of her for its own message.

situation: 上周我搬家，我爸从老家开了六个小时车过来，两天里帮我把柜子全装好，换了漏水的水龙头，走的时候还把冰箱塞满了饺子。我们家平时不太说这些话，想发微信好好谢谢他。
reply: 爸，到家了吧？这次搬家多亏您，开六个小时车过来，两天就把柜子全装好了，漏水的龙头也换了，要是我一个人，不知道得折腾多久。今天打开冰箱，满满都是您包的饺子，一下子觉得这个新家有家的样子了。谢谢爸。
note: 家里越不常说谢谢，越要具体：他做了什么、帮你省了什么、给你带来什么感觉，不附带任何请求。

situation: I'm a wedding photographer. The bride, Mariana, just texted that the photos of her grandmother dancing made the whole family cry and that I was 'the best decision of the wedding'. I want to thank her without false modesty, and without sliding in a request for a review.
reply: Mariana, what a lovely message, thank you. I'm so glad the moments with your grandmother came through, and hearing they made everyone cry means a lot. It was a joy to photograph a day with that much love in it.
note: Accept it and stop: no bounce-back and no ask. If you want a review, ask in a separate message a few days later.

situation: After my quarterly forecast presentation, a senior colleague, Derek, posted in the team Slack channel: 'wow, that was actually really good, didn't expect that from you!'. The forecast section took me two weeks. I want to reply without being prickly or letting the dig slide into how people see me.
reply: Thanks, Derek. The forecast section took a couple of weeks to get right, so I'm glad it landed.
note: A backhanded compliment: take the compliment, ignore the dig, and name the work. If the pattern repeats, raise it with him privately, not in the channel.

situation: 周会上领导表扬了这次销售报表按时上线，但没提到实习生小杨。其实她花了两周，把三年的历史订单数据一条条清洗对齐，我们后面做分析几乎没返工。想在项目群里专门夸她一下。
reply: 补充一句：这次报表能按时上线，小杨功不可没。她花了两周把三年的历史订单数据一条条清洗对齐，我们后面做分析几乎没返工。谢谢小杨！
note: 在群里替被忽略的人补上功劳：说清她具体做了什么、带来了什么效果，不带对领导的抱怨。

situation: My ex-husband Mark and I share custody of our 14-year-old, Ruby. Last Saturday, at Mark's, she got dumped by her first boyfriend, and Mark sat up with her till midnight just listening; she told me he 'didn't lecture at all'. We're civil but not warm, and I want to text him.
reply: Mark, Ruby told me about Saturday night. You sat up with her till midnight and just listened, and she said you didn't lecture at all. That was exactly what she needed, and it meant a lot to me to hear it.
note: Keeping it to what he did for Ruby stops it reading as a bid to reopen anything.

situation: 我在大理开了家民宿。住了三晚的客人王女士在订房平台上写了条长评，说管家小杨半夜帮她发烧的孩子买到了退烧药，还说'这是我住过最有人情味的民宿'。我想在评论下面公开回复她。
reply: 王女士，谢谢您写下这么用心的评价，读完我们全店都很开心。那天夜里是小杨跑出去买的药，这句'最有人情味'我会原话转告她。祝孩子健健康康，一家人都好。
note: 公开回复好评：先大方接住，再把功劳点名给具体的人，不顺带打广告，也不邀请再订。

situation: On a two-hour train from York to London, the dad across the aisle had a toddler melting down for most of the trip. He stayed completely calm, quietly singing to her the whole time and never snapping. We're both getting off at King's Cross and I'd like to say something kind to him without it being weird.
reply: Just wanted to say, you were so patient with her the whole way from York, singing her through all of it. Genuinely impressive. Have a good rest of your day.
note: To a stranger, in person: name what they did, then go; don't wait around for a reply.

situation: I'm Korean-American and grew up in Ohio. After our kickoff call, the new client lead, Greg, wrote in the shared Slack channel: 'Great session, and your English is really impressive!' I don't want to lecture him, but I don't want to just say thanks either. The next step is sending him the rollout timeline on Friday.
reply: Thanks, Greg, glad the session was useful! I'd hope the English holds up, I grew up in Ohio. I'll send the rollout timeline on Friday.
note: Accept the part that's a compliment, correct the assumption in one light clause, and move to the work.

situation: 同组的小林这次升了主管，我也申请了这个位置，没选上。她上个月带着两个新人把拖了两个月的系统迁移按时做完了，我是真心佩服。想在微信上私下跟她说一句，不想显得酸。
reply: 小林，恭喜升主管！上个月那个拖了两个月的系统迁移，你带着两个新人按时做完了，我是真心佩服。这个位置你当得起。
note: 夸一起竞争过的人：只说她做成的具体事和你的真实感受，不提自己落选，也不加“虽然”“没想到”之类的转折。

situation: Mark, a colleague on another team, keeps commenting on my looks in Teams chats: 'nice dress today' last week, and today 'you should wear your hair down more often'. Last week I replied 'ha, thanks, anyway about the report' and it didn't stop. We still have to finish the vendor review together by Friday 9 October.
reply: Mark, I'd rather you didn't comment on my appearance. Let's keep it to the work. Where are we on the vendor review for Friday?
note: The light deflection already failed, so say it plainly once; if it continues, keep the messages and take it to your manager or HR.

situation: 日本の会社で働いています。今日の取引先への提案のあと、部長が他部署の人もいる前で「田中さんの資料、すごく分かりやすかった」と褒めてくれたのに、その場で思わず「いえいえ、全然です」と言ってしまいました。価格の比較表は3回作り直したので本当は嬉しかったです。あとで社内チャットで一言きちんとお礼を伝えたいです。
reply: 部長、本日はありがとうございました。皆さんの前で資料を褒めていただき、本当に嬉しかったです。特に価格の比較表は3回作り直したので、伝わってよかったです。
note: 謙遜が普通の職場でも、その場で打ち消してしまったら、後からお礼と一言の受け止めで十分に取り戻せる。

situation: 家里洗衣机不排水，我照着B站上一位UP主“老周修家电”的视频，自己拆开清了排水泵，里面卡着一枚硬币，二十分钟就修好了。他视频里每一步都拍得很清楚，开头还专门提醒先拔电源。我从没拆过家电，想在视频下面留言夸夸他。
reply: 照着这个视频修好了我家洗衣机！排水泵拆开果然卡着一枚硬币，二十分钟搞定。您每一步都拍得特别清楚，开头还专门提醒先拔电源，我这个从没拆过家电的人也敢动手了。谢谢老周！
note: 夸陌生人也要具体：他做了什么、帮你做成了什么，不顺带提要求或催更。

situation: Mein Freund Jonas ist seit heute ein Jahr ohne Alkohol. In unserer WhatsApp-Gruppe hat er es nur mit einem Daumen-Emoji erwähnt, er mag kein großes Theater. In diesem Jahr ist er jeden Samstagmorgen mit mir laufen gegangen, statt freitags lange in der Kneipe zu sitzen. Ich will ihm privat schreiben.
reply: Jonas, ein Jahr. Ich mache kein Theater draus, versprochen, nur eins: Dass du dieses Jahr jeden Samstagmorgen mit mir laufen warst, statt freitags in der Kneipe zu sitzen, hat mir gezeigt, wie ernst du es meinst. Ich bin stolz auf dich.
note: Die Mühe loben, nicht das Aussehen; privat statt in der Gruppe, ohne Ratschläge und ohne Fragen dazu.

situation: 国庆在婆婆家，第一次在她面前包饺子。婆婆尝了一个说“比我包得还好吃”。按习惯我差点说“哪里哪里”，其实馅是照着她上回教的方法调的，我在家练了三次，被夸挺高兴的。
reply: 谢谢妈！我在家练了三次，听您这么说真高兴。馅是照着您上回教的方法调的，您教得好。
note: 长辈夸你时先接住再归功，比一句“哪里哪里”更让对方觉得自己的夸奖被当真。

situation: I'm Sarah Lindqvist. In my final year of high school, in 2006, my chemistry teacher, Mr. Okafor, stayed after school every Tuesday to walk me through equilibrium problems, and once told me I had 'a chemist's patience'. I've been a hospital pharmacist for twelve years now. I just found his email on the school website and want to thank him, 20 years late.
reply: Dear Mr. Okafor, you may not remember me: Sarah Lindqvist, class of 2006. In my final year you stayed after school every Tuesday to walk me through equilibrium problems until they clicked, and you told me I had a chemist's patience. I've been a hospital pharmacist for twelve years now, and I don't think I'd have chosen it without those Tuesdays. Thank you.
note: Years later, the specific thing plus what it led to is the whole message; no ask, and no reply needed.

situation: My cousin Rachel gave the eulogy at our grandad Harold's funeral on Saturday. She told the story of him stalling his old green van on purpose while teaching her to drive, so she'd stop being scared of stalling, and the whole room laughed through their tears. I want to text her, knowing she's exhausted and grieving too.
reply: Rachel, I keep thinking about your eulogy on Saturday. The story about Grandad stalling the green van on purpose so you'd stop being scared was so completely him, and hearing the whole room laugh through the tears was the first moment that day I felt okay. No need to reply, I just wanted you to know.
note: To someone grieving: one specific moment and its effect on you, nothing asked, and the reply made explicitly optional.

situation: In July I argued against my colleague Lena's idea to move our customer newsletter from Friday afternoons to Tuesday mornings, and the team went with her. The September numbers are in: open rates went from 22% to 31%. I want to tell her on Slack that she was right.
reply: Lena, the September numbers are in: open rates went from 22% to 31% since the newsletter moved to Tuesday mornings. I argued against it in July, and you were right. That was a smart call, nice work.
note: Name the result, own your earlier objection in one line, and stop there so she doesn't have to manage an apology.

situation: My younger brother Dan, 26, became a dad four months ago and worries he won't be a good one. At Sunday lunch, when baby Ivy started screaming, he took her outside and walked her up and down the garden for 40 minutes so his wife Mei could finally eat a hot meal. I want to text him.
reply: Dan, watching you walk Ivy up and down the garden for 40 minutes on Sunday so Mei could eat a hot meal has stuck with me. That's the kind of dad she's got. Really proud of you.
note: Name the choice he made, not a trait, and leave his worry unmentioned; the compliment answers it.

situation: I'm Ms Clarke and I teach Year 4. At lunch today Amir, who is usually very quiet, noticed our new pupil Lily sitting on her own, went over by himself and spent the whole break teaching her the playground clapping game. I want to email his parents, Mr and Mrs Haddad, just to tell them.
reply:
Dear Mr and Mrs Haddad,
I wanted to share something lovely from today. At lunch, Amir noticed that our new pupil, Lily, was sitting on her own, and he went over all by himself and spent the whole break teaching her the playground clapping game. It was such a kind thing to do, and it made my day. You should be very proud of him.
Best wishes,
Ms Clarke
note: A note home with no 'but' and no ask: the specific act and its effect, so it gets read out at the dinner table.

situation: My 16-year-old daughter Mia, who's rarely mushy, texted me after I spoke at her school's careers day: 'ngl you were actually the best one, my friends said you were cool'. I was nervous about embarrassing her in front of her friends, and I usually joke these things away.
reply: Thank you, Mia, that genuinely made my day. I was nervous about embarrassing you in front of your friends, so I'm really glad it went well.
note: Receiving praise from your teenager: accept it plainly, with no joke and no fuss, so she feels safe saying it again.

situation: Le pedí a mi amiga Lucía que fuera mi testigo de boda y anoche me contestó por WhatsApp, con mucho cariño, que este año está tan desbordada que no podría darle al papel lo que merece, pero que quiere estar en la boda como invitada. Me dolió un poco, pero valoro mucho que me lo dijera de frente en vez de aceptar y agobiarse. Quiero decírselo.
reply: Lucía, gracias por decírmelo así, de frente y con tanto cariño. Sé que no era fácil, y me dice mucho de ti que prefirieras ser sincera antes que aceptar y agobiarte. Me hace muchísima ilusión que estés en la boda, y eso es lo que de verdad importa.
note: Elogiar la sinceridad de un no: lo concreto que hizo y su efecto, sin pedirle nada ni intentar que cambie de idea.

situation: 我在国外读书。我妈今年68岁，上个月自己报了社区老年大学的手机课，学会了视频通话，昨天第一次主动给我打了视频，还自己把美颜调好了。想发微信夸夸她，又怕说得像哄小孩。
reply: 妈，昨天您主动给我打视频，我高兴了一整晚。手机课是您自己报名、一节一节学下来的，连美颜都会自己调了，我真佩服您。以后想我了随时打，我都接。
note: 夸长辈学新东西：说她付出的努力和对你的意义，别用“没想到”“真厉害呀”这种哄孩子的口气。

situation: I posted a photo of the cabled sweater I finished after three months in a knitting Discord server. A guy I've never talked to DMed me: 'gorgeous sweater, but the girl wearing it is even better, are you single?' I'm not interested and just want to keep it about knitting.
reply: Thanks, the sweater took me three months. I'm just here for the knitting, so I'll leave it there.
note: Short, closed and nothing to build on; if he messages again, don't reply, and use the server's block and report tools.

situation: Last Friday at 6pm my report Tomás spotted that the payroll file he'd prepared had the wrong overtime rate for 14 people. He flagged it to me straight away, fixed it before the 8pm cut-off, and nobody was paid wrong. He's seemed quiet and embarrassed since, and I want to message him on Slack.
reply: Tomás, about last Friday: you caught the overtime rate yourself, told me straight away and fixed it before the 8pm cut-off, so all 14 people were paid right. That's exactly what I want anyone on this team to do when something goes wrong, and it's a big part of why I trust your work.
note: Praise the choice to flag it, with no 'but' and no lesson attached, so the next mistake gets raised just as fast.

situation: 我30岁，上个月刚当上客服主管。组里的张姐45岁，干了十二年。上周有位客户为退货在电话里吵了二十分钟，我当时就在旁边，张姐一直没抬高声音，最后把退款和换货两个办法讲清楚让客户自己选，客户挂电话前还跟她道了谢。想在微信上私下夸她一句，又怕显得像在居高临下地打分。
reply: 张姐，上周那通退货电话我在旁边听完了。客户吵了二十分钟，您一直没抬高声音，最后把退款和换货两个办法讲清楚让他自己选，他挂电话前还跟您道了谢。这一招我得好好学。
note: 夸比自己资深的人，也是说具体做法和效果；用“我得学”代替“做得不错”，就不像在打分。

situation: My mum died last month, and I gave the eulogy at her funeral on Saturday; I rewrote it four times. Her oldest friend, Pat, texted today: 'Your eulogy was perfect, she'd have been so proud of you.' I'm exhausted, and I usually brush these things off.
reply: Thank you, Pat. That means so much, especially coming from you. I rewrote it four times trying to get her right, so I'm really glad to hear it.
note: Receiving praise while grieving: accept it plainly, no bounce-back, and no need to open a longer conversation than you have energy for.
